claims.statement: Coverage A in both HO-3 edition 2011-05 and HO-3 edition 2018-09 covers the declared-residence dwelling, attached structures, and on- or next-to-premises materials and supplies used to construct, alter, or repair it; under 2018-09, Coverage A and B insure against direct physical loss except as excluded in Section I.

HO-3 edition 2011-05 remains the governing form for policies written under it, regardless of when a loss is reported, while HO-3 edition 2018-09 supersedes it for policies written on or after 2018-09-01; settlement must start with the policy's issued edition.

HO-3 editions 2011-05 and 2018-09 condition Coverage A replacement-cost settlement on the dwelling being insured to at least 80 percent of its replacement cost at the time of loss; 2018-09 A.3 additionally makes that baseline subject to A.4 roof-surfacing provisions, and neither A.3 states a below-threshold settlement formula.

For a HO-3 edition 2011-05 policy, A.3 expressly includes roof surfacing in replacement-cost settlement subject to the applicable deductible and 80-percent condition, and supplies no separate roof-surfacing settlement basis.

For a HO-3 edition 2018-09 policy, A.4 settles windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing loss at replacement cost unless an actual-cash-value roof schedule endorsement is attached; only an attached endorsement governs settlement for roof surfacing, while all other dwelling components continue under A.3.

Underwriting guidance can restrict whether HO 23 74 is bound but is not policy contract language; for example, the Texas guide requires it for roofs aged 15 years or more at new business and renewal, while the authority matrix identifies the guidance as internal and limits binding authority.

For HO-3 edition 2018-09, Coverage A and B insure against direct physical loss except Section I exclusions; A.3 provides replacement-cost dwelling settlement subject to A.4, the applicable deductible, and the 80-percent replacement-cost insurance condition.

HO-3 2018-09 A.4 leaves windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing loss at replacement cost unless an actual-cash-value roof schedule endorsement is attached; when attached, that endorsement governs roof surfacing only and other dwelling components remain under A.3.

Attached HO 23 74 edition 2018-09 defines roof surfacing as specified exterior surfacing materials plus directly underlying underlayment and flashing, excludes deck, trusses, rafters, sheathing, and interior finish, and therefore preserves replacement-cost settlement for those other dwelling components.

Under HO 23 74 R.2, only windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing loss is settled at actual cash value using the R.3 schedule less the applicable deductible; roof-surfacing loss from another covered peril remains replacement cost and is outside the endorsement.

HO 23 74 determines its payable percentage by roof-surfacing material and age at loss; it uses documented original-installation or most recent full-replacement date, presumes dwelling age if undocumented, does not reset age for a partial repair, and permits slope-specific age after full slope replacement.
HO 23 74 R.4 imposes a 25-percent minimum payable amount for roof surfacing before the applicable deductible, so the schedule calculation and floor precede deductible application.

HO-3 2018-09 S.5 applies the Declarations deductible to each Section I loss and otherwise selects only the larger when a required state windstorm-or-hail deductible also applies; for an attached and applicable Texas HO 01 45 2022-01, T.1 expressly amends S.5, implements Bulletin B-2021-08, and instead selects only the separate windstorm-and-hail deductible for windstorm/hail loss, with allocation rules for separable and inseparable mixed-peril loss.

HO 23 74 R.6 preserves HO-3 2018-09 Exclusion D.1 as the separate boundary for code-required undamaged roof-surfacing replacement, rather than making it a roof-schedule benefit; separately, attached HO 04 16 O.1/O.3 may write back D.1 for the eligible additional incurred cost after damaged-property settlement, subject to its distinct limit and completion conditions.

For applicable Florida policies, OIR-2023-04 separately regulates roof-age underwriting and inspection practices and F.4 constrains offers and application of a roof deductible or ACV schedule, including barring an ACV schedule for a roof under ten years old at policy effective date; the bulletin does not itself attach endorsements or change the A.4 and attached HO 23 74 settlement terms of an issued policy.

For Florida losses, OIR-2023-04 provides that a hurricane deductible and separate roof deductible may not both be applied to the same loss and requires only the larger; it also imposes nonrenewal notice and annual roof-condition reporting obligations that are distinct from contractual settlement terms.

The roof-claim handling guide is expressly internal rather than policy language; it operationalizes documentation, scope separation, and referral triggers for roof claims without changing the issued contract settlement terms.

HO-3 2018-09 retains insured loss duties and a payment condition across roof settlement paths: prompt notice, protection from further damage, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, and payment 60 days after proof of loss plus written agreement, appraisal award, or court judgment.

HO-3 edition 2011-05 remains governing for policies written under it regardless of reporting date, while multistate HO-3 edition 2018-09 supersedes it for policies written on or after 2018-09-01; the later Coverage B changes must not be retroactively applied to a 2011-05 policy.

Under HO-3 2018-09 Section I B.1, Coverage B includes other structures on the defined residence premises that are separated by clear space or connected to the dwelling only by a fence, utility line, or similar connection; HO-3 2011-05 B.1 contains only the clear-space formulation.
Both HO-3 2011-05 B.2 and HO-3 2018-09 B.2 set Coverage B at 10% of the Coverage A limit as additional insurance.

HO-3 2018-09 B.3 does not cover an other structure rented or held for rental to a person who is not a tenant of the dwelling, unless it is used solely as a private garage; this B.3 limitation is absent from the supplied HO-3 2011-05 Coverage B text.

For HO-3 2018-09, Coverage B property is insured only against direct physical loss except as excluded by Section I, so meeting the structure scope and having a 10% limit does not by itself establish coverage.

The HO-3 2018-09 Section I water, earth-movement, neglect and deterioration, ordinance-or-law, and intentional-loss exclusions constrain Coverage B losses; the water exclusions A.1 through A.3 apply regardless of another contributing cause or event.

When HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 is attached, W.1 writes back the HO-3 A.3 sewer/drain and sump backup, overflow, or discharge exclusion for direct physical loss to Coverage B property, including an event resulting from equipment mechanical breakdown.

Under attached HO 04 90 edition 2010-10, the water-backup benefit has a $5,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless a higher limit is shown, is part of the Coverage B limit, uses a separate $500 deductible, retains the policy settlement basis for Coverage B, and is subject to its known-maintenance-failure condition.

Attached HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 provides limited Coverage B fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria coverage only when it results from a Section I insured peril during the policy period; it writes back HO-3 2018-09 C.2 only to that extent and leaves the identified underlying water and seepage exclusions operative.

The attached HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 fungi benefit is a $10,000 per-policy-period aggregate unless a higher limit is shown, is part of rather than additional to Coverage B, includes the specified removal and access costs, and separately requires mitigation of known or reasonably knowable water intrusion.

When HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 is attached, O.1 writes back HO-3 2018-09 D.1 only for increased cost actually incurred to repair, rebuild, or demolish a damaged other structure due to an ordinance or law in force at loss and only where the underlying Section I loss is covered; it is not a write-back for an otherwise excluded cause of loss.

The attached HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 ordinance-or-law benefit is additional insurance of 10% of Coverage A unless a higher percentage is shown and does not reduce Coverage B; it is payable only after damaged-property settlement, for costs actually incurred within its completion deadline and subject to its retained exclusions.

For HO-3 2018-09 Section I claims, the insured must give prompt notice, protect property from further damage, and submit a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request; the declarations deductible applies to each Section I loss subject to the state-endorsed windstorm-or-hail rule.
HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 W.4 separately preserves the HO-3 A.1 exclusion for flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, storm surge, and overflow of a body of water.
HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 W.4 separately preserves the HO-3 A.2 exclusion for water below the surface of the ground.

HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it regardless of when loss is reported, while edition 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01; the exact attached endorsement edition must therefore be identified before applying water-backup terms.

When HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 is attached to a compatible selected HO-3 policy, W.1 supplies the narrow direct-physical-loss write-back for the selected base form's A.3 sewer/drain-backup or sump-equipment overflow/discharge exclusion, including an event resulting from equipment mechanical breakdown.
HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.1 exclusion for flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, storm surge, and overflow of a body of water.
HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.2 exclusion for water below the surface of the ground, including the specified pressure, seepage, and leakage routes.

For loss covered under attached HO 04 90 edition 2026-01, W.2 sets a $10,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless higher declared, within rather than additional to the A/B/C limits; W.3 applies a separate $1,000 deductible instead of the Section I deductible; and W.7 retains the attached policy's Coverage B settlement basis.

HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 retains the W.5 known-and-unremedied maintenance condition and adds W.6: if the residence premises has finished area below grade, endorsement coverage requires an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device on the serving sewer line at the time of loss; W.6 did not appear in edition 2010-10.

Florida and Texas water-backup appetite guides are non-contractual underwriting guidance with battery-backed-sump-pump criteria at specified below-grade and higher-limit binding thresholds; those criteria do not establish, replace, or add the HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.6 backflow-prevention condition.

HO-3 edition 2011-05 remains controlling for policies written under it despite being superseded for policies written on or after 2018-09-01; HO-3 edition 2018-09 governs new policies from that date, so Coverage C special-limit changes cannot be applied retroactively.

Both HO-3 editions extend Coverage C to personal property owned or used by an insured anywhere in the world, while HO-3 2018-09 separately restricts Coverage C to direct physical loss caused only by its listed P.2 perils and remains subject to Section I exclusions.

Both HO-3 2011-05 C.2 and 2018-09 C.2 settle personal property at actual cash value at the time of loss unless a replacement cost personal property endorsement is attached; actual cash value deducts depreciation and replacement cost does not, with 2018-09 specifying age, condition, and remaining useful life for depreciation.

Coverage C special limits changed from HO-3 2011-05 to 2018-09: watercraft and theft of jewelry each rose from $1,000 to $1,500; theft of firearms rose from $2,000 to $2,500; 2018-09 added a $2,500 residence-premises business-property category; money and precious metals remained at $200. The 2018-09 special limits do not increase the Coverage C limit.

When HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 is attached, it writes back specified sewer or drain backup and sump-related loss subject to a $5,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless increased in the Declarations, a separate $500 deductible, continuing flood/surface/subsurface-water exclusions, and a known-unremedied-maintenance condition; Coverage C property is settled at actual cash value regardless of a replacement-cost personal-property endorsement unless the endorsement Declarations say otherwise.

An attached HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 writes back limited Coverage C loss from fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria only when it results from a Section I insured peril during the policy period; it leaves the stated flood, surface-water, subsurface-water, and continuous-seepage exclusions in place.

HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 has a $10,000 aggregate-per-policy-period limit unless increased in the Declarations, is part of the Coverage C limit, includes specified removal, access, testing, and related Coverage D costs, and withholds loss to the stated extent of failure to mitigate known or reasonably knowable water intrusion.

HO-3 2011-05 requires prompt notice, protection from further damage, and sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request; 2018-09 adds an inventory of damaged personal property. Each applies the Section I deductible to each loss, subject in 2018-09 to its stated state-amendatory windstorm-or-hail rule.

When attached, HO 04 90 (2010-10) W.1 writes back the selected HO-3 A.3 water-backup exclusion for the described sewer/drain and sump events, including an event that results from mechanical breakdown of the equipment.
HO 04 81 (2018-09) M.5 imposes its reasonable water-intrusion mitigation condition independently of the HO-3 C.1 neglect exclusion, so the M.5 limitation can apply whether or not C.1 applies.

HO 04 81 is a limited C.2 write-back rather than a replacement-cost personal-property endorsement: after its M.1–M.5 coverage gates, the otherwise applicable Coverage C settlement terms and other policy provisions remain in force.

HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 replaces edition 2010-10 for policies written on or after 2026-01-01. For covered loss under the 2026 edition, W.2 has a $10,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless increased in the Declarations and remains within the applicable A/B/C limit; W.3 applies a separate $1,000 deductible in place of the Section I Declarations deductible; and W.7 settles Coverage C property at actual cash value despite a replacement-cost personal-property endorsement unless the Declarations state otherwise.

Only HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.6 adds an eligibility condition for residence premises with a finished area below grade: an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device must have been on the serving sewer line at the time of loss. The form states this requirement is new and absent from edition 2010-10.
HO-3 2018-09 supersedes HO-3 2011-05 only for policies written on or after 2018-09-01; HO-3 2011-05 remains controlling for policies written under it regardless of when a loss is reported.

Under both HO-3 editions, Coverage D requires a covered loss that makes the residence premises not fit to live in and pays only the reasonable increase in living expenses necessary to maintain the insured's normal standard of living.

For HO-3 2018-09, the Section I direct-physical-loss grant for Coverage A and B remains subject to Section I exclusions, so Coverage D's covered-loss prerequisite does not itself displace the applicable coverage and exclusion analysis.
Both HO-3 2011-05 D.2 and HO-3 2018-09 D.2 set Coverage D's limit of liability at 20% of the Coverage A limit.

HO-3 2018-09 D.1 limits qualifying Coverage D expenses to the shortest time reasonably required to repair or replace the premises; the supplied HO-3 2011-05 D.1 has no corresponding shortest-time qualification.

When attached, HO 04 81 2018-09 M.1 provides limited direct physical-loss coverage for fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria only when it results from a Section I insured peril during the policy period, writing back HO-3 2018-09 Section I Exclusion C.2 only to that extent.

HO 04 81 2018-09 M.4 modifies accounting for a qualifying Coverage D loss-of-use increase attributable to fungi, rot, or bacteria by including it in the M.3 aggregate; it does not independently grant additional living expenses, so HO-3 2018-09 D.1 prerequisites and D.2's 20% Coverage A limit remain operative. M.3 is $10,000 per policy period unless the Declarations show a higher limit and is part of the applicable Coverage A, B, and C limits.

HO 04 81 2018-09 does not restore fungi-related coverage where the underlying moisture source is excluded flood, surface water, subsurface water, or continuous/repeated seepage, and it withholds endorsement coverage to the extent the insured failed to take reasonable water-intrusion mitigation steps after actual or constructive knowledge.

The issued HO-3 edition controls Section II coverage and exclusions: 2011-05 remains governing for policies written under it regardless of later reporting, while 2018-09 supersedes it for policies written on or after 2018-09-01.

Both supplied HO-3 editions define an occurrence as an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions, resulting in bodily injury or property damage during the policy period.

Under E.1 in both HO-3 editions, when a claim or suit seeks damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an applicable occurrence, the insurer will pay up to its liability limit damages for which the insured is legally liable and provide a defense at its expense.

Under F.1 in both HO-3 editions, Coverage F promises necessary medical expenses incurred or medically ascertained within three years of the accident causing bodily injury to a person other than an insured.

HO-3 2018-09 F.1 adds that Coverage F bodily injury must arise out of a condition on the insured location or be caused by an insured's activities; the supplied 2011-05 F.1 does not contain that qualification.

Both HO-3 editions exclude Coverage E and F bodily injury or property damage arising from an insured's business activities, but 2018-09 L.1 excepts occasional rental of the residence premises for fewer than 15 days in a policy year and 2011-05 L.1 has no stated rental exception.

In both supplied HO-3 editions, L.2 excludes Coverage E and F for bodily injury or property damage arising from ownership, maintenance, or use of a motor vehicle, watercraft over 25 horsepower, or aircraft.
HO-3 2018-09 L.3 adds a Coverage E-only exclusion for property damage to property owned by or rented to an insured; the supplied 2011-05 Section II exclusions contain L.1 and L.2 only.

HO 04 81 2018-09 supplies a limited Section I fungi, rot, or bacteria property write-back, but M.6 does not provide, extend, or modify Section II liability coverage; attachment therefore leaves the governing HO-3 Coverage E/F grants and Section II exclusions in effect for a related bodily-injury or property-damage demand.

The Texas appetite guide and cross-state referral matrix require referral and a completed liability supplement before binding when a prior liability claim involves a dog bite, trampoline, or unfenced pool; as internal guidance, those requirements constrain underwriting review rather than modify issued Section II coverage or add a policy exclusion.

The corpus issues revisions as new frozen form files rather than altering prior operative text, and HO-3 2011-05 remains the governing form for losses under policies written under that edition even when reported later.

For multistate HO-3 policies, edition 2011-05 applies to policies written on or after 2011-05-01 until it is prospectively superseded for policies written on or after 2018-09-01, which are governed by edition 2018-09.

The HO-3 forms make water-backup and 2018 wind-or-hail roof-surfacing exceptions conditional on the relevant endorsement being attached, so the endorsement wording alone is not evidence that it is part of an individual policy.

HO 01 45 edition 2022-01 applies only to a Texas HO-3 policy to which it attaches and whose effective date is on or after 2022-01-01; where it conflicts with the attached base form, the Texas endorsement governs.

For a 2011-05 HO-3 policy, Coverage A including roof surfacing is settled at replacement cost with no separate roof-surfacing basis, whereas a 2018-09 policy makes dwelling settlement subject to A.4 and permits an attached ACV roof schedule to govern only windstorm- or hail-caused roof surfacing.

HO-3 2018-09 expressly insures Coverage A and B against direct physical loss except exclusions and restricts Coverage C to listed perils; it also broadens specified Coverage B connections and limitations and changes Coverage C special limits compared with 2011-05.

HO-3 2018-09 adds an anti-concurrent or sequential-cause rule for its water exclusions and separately excludes long-term seepage or leakage while preserving loss that is sudden and accidental as defined; those provisions are absent from the corresponding 2011-05 water and deterioration exclusions.

HO-3 2018-09 adds an ordinance-or-law exclusion unless an ordinance endorsement is attached and applies intentional loss to all insureds, while its 2011-05 counterpart has neither that ordinance exclusion nor the all-insureds intentional-loss wording.

HO-3 2018-09 adds a personal-property inventory duty, states loss-adjustment and payment timing, and supplies a default routing rule for a separate state-required windstorm-or-hail deductible; 2011-05 instead has only the general Section I deductible provision.

HO-3 2018-09 changes Section II by conditioning medical payments on insured-location or insured-activity causation, allowing the stated occasional-rental exception to the business exclusion, and excluding Coverage E property damage to insured-owned or rented property.

When attached to a policy written under it, HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 W.1 writes back the HO-3 A.3 water-backup exclusion with limited A/B/C coverage for the stated backup or sump events, while W.4 preserves the A.1 flood/surface-water and A.2 subsurface-water exclusions; W.2-W.3, W.5, and W.6 impose its sublimit, separate deductible, maintenance condition, and settlement rules.

When attached, HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 provides limited Section I fungi, wet-or-dry-rot, or bacteria coverage only when the condition results from an underlying insured peril; it retains the stated underlying water exclusions, has an aggregate policy-period limit and mitigation condition, and does not modify Section II liability coverage.

When attached to a 2018-09 HO-3 policy, HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 overrides Exclusion D.1 for its stated ordinance-or-law costs on a covered underlying Section I loss, including stated undamaged portions, but is separately limited and payable only for timely incurred increased cost after damaged-property settlement.

When attached to a 2018-09 HO-3 policy, HO 23 74 edition 2018-09 changes only windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing settlement to actual cash value under its material-and-age schedule and 25-percent pre-deductible floor; non-surfacing components and other covered-peril surfacing losses remain on the base-form replacement-cost path.

HO 23 74 does not pay ordinance-required replacement of undamaged roof surfacing unless an ordinance-or-law endorsement is attached; HO 04 16 is the endorsement that can cover that stated additional work subject to its own requirements.

For an attached qualifying Texas HO 01 45 endorsement, windstorm-or-hail loss receives only the separate windstorm-and-hail deductible, the form controls percentage and mixed-peril rules, and it also changes the Section I action period and sets claim acknowledgement, decision, and payment deadlines.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 separately requires stated deductible application, disclosure, and filing controls for Texas residential-property policies effective on or after 2022-01-01, but those regulatory requirements do not establish that a particular contractual endorsement was attached.

The repository's inventory of frozen-authority forms establishes document availability, not that an endorsement was issued with a specific policy; policy assembly must verify the endorsement's attachment and edition in the issued policy record or Declarations before treating it as contract text.

HO-3 base-form selection and HO 04 90 endorsement-edition selection use distinct written-date rules: the 2018-09 HO-3 supersedes the 2011-05 form for policies written on or after 2018-09-01, while HO 04 90 2026-01 replaces 2010-10 for policies written on or after 2026-01-01 and 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it.

For an attached HO 04 90 edition 2026-01, W.1 writes back HO-3 A.3 and W.4 preserves A.1 and A.2; W.2 sets a $10,000 default policy-period sublimit within A/B/C limits, W.3 substitutes a $1,000 separate deductible, W.6 requires an installed and operable backflow-prevention device at loss when the residence has finished below-grade area, and W.7 uses the policy settlement basis for A/B and actual cash value for C unless the endorsement Declarations state otherwise.

HO-3 2011-05 governs policies written on or after 2011-05-01 that were written before the 2018 edition and continues to govern adjustment of losses under those policies regardless of report date; HO-3 2018-09 governs policies written on or after 2018-09-01, so 2018-only conditions cannot be imported into a 2011 policy.

Under HO-3 2011-05, Section I S.1 requires prompt notice to the insurer or agent and protection from further damage, S.2 requires a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after insurer request, S.3 requires full compliance and suit within two years after loss, and S.4 applies the Declarations deductible to each Section I loss.

Under HO-3 2018-09, S.1 retains prompt notice and protection duties and adds an inventory of damaged personal property; S.2 retains the request-triggered 60-day sworn-proof requirement; and S.4 keeps the full-compliance and two-year action limitation.

The HO-3 2018-09 base-form payment provision is S.3: payment is due 60 days after receipt of proof of loss and written agreement, an appraisal award, or a court judgment, while 2011-05 S.1-S.4 contains no corresponding payment provision.
Both HO-3 editions exclude loss caused by neglect, defined as failure to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property at and after loss, reinforcing their S.1 property-protection duties.

HO-3 2018-09 S.5 applies the Declarations deductible to each Section I loss, recognizes a separate state-required windstorm or hail deductible, and directs that only the larger is deducted where both apply.

For loss covered under a verified attached HO 04 90 endorsement, W.3 modifies rather than stacks with the selected base Section I Declarations deductible: 2010-10 applies a separate $500 deductible to each endorsement loss and 2026-01 applies a separate $1,000 deductible.

For a Texas HO 01 45 endorsement effective on or after 2022-01-01, T.1 implements Bulletin B-2021-08 by applying a separate windstorm/hail deductible expressed as a Coverage A percentage generally limited to 1%-5%, with a 10% seacoast maximum; the bulletin also permits a flat-dollar alternative no lower than the all-other-perils deductible.

Texas HO 01 45 and Bulletin B-2021-08 prohibit applying both the windstorm/hail and all-other-perils deductibles to the same wind/hail loss; for a mixed-peril occurrence, each deductible applies only to separately determinable damage, otherwise only the larger single deductible applies, and an unnotified renewal increase is ineffective for that term.

For an applicable Texas HO 01 45, T.4 extends the identified S.4 action period to two years and one day after loss, while T.5 separately requires acknowledgement within 15 days, written approval or denial within 15 business days after all reasonably requested items, and payment within five business days after approval notice; the T.4 S.4 cross-reference matches 2018-09's action section but not 2011-05's.

A Texas per-named-storm deductible period starts when the National Hurricane Center names the storm and ends 72 hours after designation is discontinued, with all wind/hail loss in that period treated as one occurrence; where wind/hail is excluded for Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage using the specified exclusion process, HO 01 45 T.1 does not apply.

For Florida personal residential policies issued or renewed on or after 2023-07-01, a separate roof deductible requires an offer of a policy without it at a filed and approved rate plus written premium-difference disclosure; an ACV roof schedule cannot apply to a roof under 10 years old, and a hurricane and separate roof deductible cannot both be applied to the same loss, for which only the larger is deducted.

Both HO-3 editions make the Section I A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event exception dependent on attached HO 04 90; once attachment is verified, the 2010-10 endorsement remains applicable to policies written under it, while 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01, independently of the base HO-3 edition selection.
HO 04 90 W.2 sets a default within-limit policy-period sublimit of $5,000 in 2010-10 and $10,000 in 2026-01 unless the endorsement Declarations state a higher limit.

Both HO 04 90 editions deny coverage where the stated known, causative, unremedied maintenance failure is established under W.5; in 2026-01 only, W.6 additionally makes coverage for a residence with finished area below grade conditional on an installed and operable serving-sewer backflow-prevention device at the time of loss.

The water-loss guide is internal claims guidance rather than policy authority and must not be quoted to an insured or claimant; its source-first investigation instruction does not alter the selected endorsement's contractual terms.

HO 04 81 (2018-09) is an HO-3 endorsement that must be attached to the issued policy; because its M.2 references the 2018 HO-3 P.2 and C.3 provisions, those cross-references must not be transplanted onto a 2011-05 policy without compatible issued-policy support.

HO-3 2018-09 Exclusion C.2 excludes deterioration, mold, and wet or dry rot, while attached HO 04 81 M.1 writes back direct physical loss to Coverage A, B, or C property caused by fungi, wet/dry rot, or bacteria only when it results from a Section I insured peril occurring during the policy period; C.2 is displaced only to that extent.

For water- or moisture-produced fungi, rot, or bacteria, HO 04 81 M.2 requires the water or moisture to come from a covered event; the endorsement does not override HO-3 flood/surface-water exclusion A.1, subsurface-water exclusion A.2, or continuous/repeated leakage exclusion C.3 that can remove the underlying loss from coverage.

For backup-related fungi, the selected attached HO 04 90 edition's W.1 writes back HO-3 A.3 separately from HO 04 81 M.1's limited write-back of HO-3 2018-09 C.2, so both endorsements require independent attachment and coverage analyses. In either HO 04 90 edition, W.4 preserves the flood/surface-water and subsurface-water exclusions, while HO 04 81 M.2 separately preserves the underlying source and duration barriers.

HO 04 81's default $10,000 limit is a policy-period aggregate for all endorsement loss regardless of occurrences, claims, or locations, unless a higher endorsement Declarations limit is shown; it is within rather than additional to Coverage A, B, and C limits and includes removal, necessary access tear-out/replacement, post-removal testing, and attributable Coverage D loss-of-use increase.

An attributable Coverage D increase included in HO 04 81 M.4 is not a freestanding loss-of-use grant: HO-3 2018-09 D.1 still requires a covered loss that makes the residence unfit to live in and measures the reasonable necessary increase in living expenses for the shortest reasonably required repair-or-replacement time.

HO 04 81 M.5 separately withholds endorsement loss to the extent it results from failure to take reasonable steps to dry, clean, or otherwise mitigate water intrusion after the insured knew or reasonably should have known of it; this is distinct from HO-3 C.1's general neglect exclusion.
HO 04 81 provides Section I property coverage only and does not provide, extend, or modify Section II liability coverage for bodily injury or property damage arising from fungi, rot, or bacteria.

Internal claims guidance treats source and duration as documented factual gates, directs specified technical referrals and reservations of rights, and expressly says it is not policy language to quote to insureds or claimants.

HO 04 81 attachment and limits are controlled at underwriting: the internal authority matrix permits line underwriters to attach the base limit and senior underwriters to bind mold limits up to $25,000, while Florida guidance requires referral and a plumbing-age disclosure for limits above the base $10,000 aggregate; those guides are non-contractual.

The HO 04 90 edition is selected independently from the HO-3 edition: 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it regardless of reporting date, while 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01; the selected edition controls its backup-route terms.

For selected HO 04 90 2026-01 coverage, W.6 adds a water-backup gate when the residence has a finished area below grade: an equivalent installed and operable backflow-prevention device must have been on the serving sewer line at the time of loss. That new gate is absent from 2010-10 and is not a term of the separate HO 04 81 fungi endorsement.

HO 04 90 payment and settlement terms must be applied by selected edition and separately from HO 04 81: 2010-10 uses a $5,000 default policy-period sublimit, $500 deductible, and W.6 settlement provision; 2026-01 uses a $10,000 default sublimit, $1,000 deductible, and W.7 settlement provision, while HO 04 81 has its own M.3 policy-period aggregate and M.5 mitigation allocation.

HO-3 edition 2018-09 applies to policies written on or after 2018-09-01. HO 04 16 and HO 23 74 are separate endorsements that attach to HO-3 but modify different provisions (D.1 and A.4, respectively), so attachment of either must be verified independently.

For an attached HO 04 16, the HO-3 D.1 exclusion is written back only for the endorsement's covered increased cost: the ordinance or law must be in force at the time of loss and the underlying Section I loss must be covered; O.1 then makes D.1 inapplicable to loss covered under the endorsement.

HO 04 16 O.2 limits payment to 10 percent of the Declarations Coverage A limit unless a higher percentage is shown, and treats that amount as additional insurance that does not reduce Coverage A or Coverage B.

HO 04 16 O.3 covers the distinct incremental cost of ordinance-required demolition and site clearance of undamaged dwelling portions and replacement of undamaged roof surfacing needed to repair or rebuild the damaged portion; together with O.1, it supplies the conditional D.1 write-back for that eligible loss under the endorsement.

Florida homeowners appetite and referral rules are internal underwriting controls rather than policy terms, while OIR-2023-04 is a regulatory overlay for Florida personal residential property policies issued or renewed on or after 2023-07-01; the bulletin does not itself attach endorsements, select a deductible, or decide coverage.

Florida base appetite is limited to owner-occupied one-family primary residences with Coverage A from $200,000 to $900,000 and insurance to at least 80% of replacement cost; masonry and masonry veneer are eligible in approved counties, while frame requires protection class 1-5 and location outside the wind-borne debris region, and seasonal or secondary residences are outside appetite.

Florida authority is $600,000 Coverage A for line underwriters and $900,000 plus one referral condition for senior underwriters; management approval is required above the senior limit, for more than one referral condition, wind-borne-debris-region frame risks, and roof-condition nonrenewals, and cleared referrals require a recorded condition, authority level, facts, and date.

An underwriting referral cannot authorize a state filing or bulletin exception or bind a risk that is outside appetite entirely; Florida specifically places a risk with three or more water claims in five years outside appetite for the entire risk.

For Florida roofs aged 15 years or more, internal guidance requires inspection before binding; for bulletin-scope policies an insurer-required inspection is insurer-paid, qualifying insured-provided F.2 inspection evidence must be accepted without a second insured-paid inspection in the policy period, and the insurer must accept Florida-licensed inspectors rather than require its own selection.

For bulletin-scope Florida issuance or renewal, roof age alone cannot be the refusal basis when a qualifying inspection within the preceding 12 months establishes at least five years remaining useful life, and a roof-condition declination must state the specific identified deficiency.

Florida underwriting must not attach HO 23 74 to a roof under 10 years old at policy effective date; an offer of a separate roof deductible or ACV schedule also requires a no-provision policy at a filed and approved rate and written premium-difference disclosure at offer, while internal guidance requires retaining the comparison quote.

The Florida effective-date roof-age gate for an ACV schedule is distinct from HO 23 74's claim-time age calculation, and an issued, attached HO 23 74 changes settlement only for windstorm- or hail-caused roof surfacing rather than other dwelling components or roof-surfacing loss from other covered perils.

A Florida roof-condition nonrenewal requires at least 120 days' written notice, a specific reason, and every relied-on inspection report; internally it also requires management approval and Compliance review before issuance, and roof-condition nonrenewals must be annually reported by county.

Florida permits line underwriting of the base HO 04 90 limit without referral, requires a battery-backed sump pump for limits over $10,000 when any finished area is below grade, requires referral above $25,000, and gives senior underwriters water-backup limit authority up to $50,000; two water claims in five years make the endorsement outside appetite and three make the entire risk outside appetite.

Only a verified attached HO 04 90 under either supplied edition provides limited water-backup rather than flood coverage: W.1 supplies the stated sewer/drain-backup and sump overflow/discharge route, W.4 preserves the flood, surface-water, storm-surge, and subsurface-water exclusions, and W.5 retains the stated known-unremedied maintenance condition.

Florida permits line underwriting of HO 04 81 at its base $10,000 aggregate; a higher limit requires referral and plumbing-age disclosure, senior authority stops at $25,000, and a prior mold claim within five years makes only the endorsement outside appetite rather than necessarily the underlying policy.

An issued HO 04 81 provides only limited Section I property coverage for fungi, rot, or bacteria resulting from a Section I insured peril during the policy period; its default $10,000 limit is a policy-period aggregate within Coverage A/B/C limits, and the endorsement does not override flood, subsurface-water, or long-duration-leakage barriers or extend Section II liability coverage.

The Florida hurricane deductible must be taken from the filing in force for the policy effective date rather than underwriter discretion or prior-year rating output; if it and a separate roof deductible both apply to one loss, only the larger may be deducted, and the bulletin does not set either amount or establish either provision on an issued policy.

For an otherwise in-appetite Florida submission, apply and count each mandatory referral condition in the enterprise matrix in addition to Florida-specific gates. The Florida 15-year roof inspection requirement and the matrix’s 20-year roof referral are independent controls; a senior underwriter may clear only one referral condition, while more than one requires management routing.

For an attached HO 04 90, the policy-written date and exact issued endorsement edition separately select its contract terms: 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it and has a $5,000 default sublimit, $500 separate deductible, and W.6 settlement provision, while 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01 and has a $10,000 default sublimit, $1,000 separate deductible, and W.7 settlement provision.

Florida's unchanged H.4 battery-backed-sump rule is a pre-bind control only for a requested limit above $10,000 with finished area below grade, whereas issued HO 04 90 2026-01 W.6 is a distinct at-loss coverage condition for any finished-below-grade premises requiring an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent device on the serving sewer line; the 2026 condition is new and does not apply to 2010-10.

Florida H.7 and Texas G.7 constrain the enterprise matrix R.2 Coverage A ceilings; state guides may tighten but never broaden enterprise authority. Separately, matrix R.4 makes a filing or bulletin violation a hard stop that referral or management approval cannot cure.

Under internal underwriting guidance, line underwriters may bind Coverage A through $800,000 and senior underwriters through $1,500,000 while clearing at most one referral condition; management is required above senior authority or for more than one condition, and Coverage A above $1,500,000 requires a property inspection.

Internal underwriting guidance treats Coverage A below 80% of estimated replacement cost as outside appetite at every authority level, relying on the selected HO-3 form's 80% replacement-cost settlement condition rather than making a policy-coverage determination.

The matrix requires referral for specified prior-loss and liability histories, residual-market wind/hail exclusion, elevated water-backup requests, and older roofs, regardless of Coverage A limit or state; the mold, seepage, and foundation triggers depend on the identified HO-3 exclusions as risk-selection inputs.

Three or more paid water claims in five years, known unrepaired structural damage, a renovation vacant more than 30 consecutive days, and a binding action that violates a state filing or bulletin are outside appetite under internal underwriting guidance and cannot be cleared by referral.

The authority matrix gives line underwriters base-limit authority to attach HO 04 90 and HO 04 81 and authority to attach HO 04 16 and HO 23 74 without matrix limit conditions; it requires referral for water-backup requests above $25,000 or above $10,000 with finished below-grade area and no battery-backed sump pump, and gives seniors water-backup authority through $50,000. These are internal routing controls, not HO 04 90 contractual default terms, which depend on the selected endorsement edition and Declarations.

Florida H.2 requires inspection before binding for roofs aged 15 years or more and constrains the matrix R.3 older-roof referral workflow by adding that pre-bind gate; H.3/H.7 require Compliance and management routing for roof-condition nonrenewal, while the bulletin's decision, offer/application, and notice controls remain independent requirements.

Every cleared referral must record the condition, clearing authority level, facts relied on, and date; an undocumented clearance is treated as unbound authority in audit, and Florida roof-condition declinations must satisfy the bulletin's specific-deficiency standard.

On a verified attached HO 04 90, either the 2010-10 or 2026-01 edition modifies HO-3 Section I Exclusion A.3 and supplies the stated sewer/drain-backup and sump-event loss route; HO-3 makes its A.3 exception attachment-dependent. The 2010-10 edition has a default $5,000 policy-period sublimit, whereas 2026-01 has a default $10,000 sublimit, in each case unless a higher limit is shown in the endorsement Declarations.

On a verified compatible attachment to HO-3 2018-09, HO 04 81 provides limited coverage for fungi, wet/dry rot, or bacteria that would otherwise be excluded by C.2, subject to its stated trigger and $10,000 aggregate unless a higher limit is shown in the Declarations.

On a verified compatible attachment to HO-3 2018-09, HO 04 16 modifies Section I Exclusion D.1 and supplies its ordinance-or-law increased-cost path, with a default 10%-of-Coverage-A limit unless the Declarations show a higher percentage.

On a verified compatible attachment to HO-3 2018-09, HO 23 74 modifies A.4; A.4 directs windstorm- or hail-caused roof-surfacing settlement to the attached schedule while other dwelling components remain under A.3.

For Florida policies within OIR-2023-04's scope, F.4 constrains the HO 23 74 offer/application path by requiring a policy-without-provision offer at a filed and approved rate and written premium-difference disclosure, and by prohibiting application of an ACV schedule to a roof under 10 years old at the policy effective date. F.4 does not attach the endorsement or modify A.4; that contract relationship arises only from verified HO 23 74 attachment.

HO 04 90 2026-01 replaces 2010-10 for policies written on or after 2026-01-01, while 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it and governs loss adjustment under those policies regardless of reporting date; selection of the endorsement edition is therefore a separate written-date and attachment check.

The 2026-01 HO 04 90 adds a finished-below-grade condition requiring an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent device on the serving sewer line at the time of loss; this contract condition is distinct from the Florida and Texas guides' battery-backed-sump underwriting criteria for higher limits.

Texas G.3 describes the HO 04 90 W.2 base sublimit as $5,000, while the 2026-01 endorsement sets a $10,000 default and replaces 2010-10 for policies written on or after 2026-01-01; the supplied guide and matrix do not state how to resolve that guide/form version mismatch.

The Texas Homeowners Appetite Guide is internal underwriting guidance rather than policy contract language; the enterprise referral matrix permits state guides to impose tighter authority but not broader authority, and a referral cannot approve a filing or bulletin violation.

Texas base appetite is owner-occupied one-family primary residences with Coverage A from $150,000 through $1,200,000, insurance of at least 80% of replacement cost, frame/masonry/masonry-veneer construction, and protection class 1-8; seasonal and secondary residences are permitted only in protection classes 1-6 with a five-year clear prior-loss record.

Texas applies a tighter state-specific Coverage A authority model: line underwriters may bind through $800,000, senior underwriters through $1,200,000 and one referral condition, and Coverage A above $1,200,000 or more than one referral condition requires management approval.

For Texas new business and renewal, roof surfacing aged 15 years or more requires HO 23 74; roof surfacing aged 25 years or more is outside appetite regardless of endorsement unless a full roof replacement is documented within 90 days of binding.

The enterprise matrix requires referral for roof surfacing age 20 years or more, which adds escalation to Texas's 15-year roof-schedule control but does not replace Texas's stricter 25-year eligibility rule.

Texas treats 14 enumerated counties as coastal for its operational roof and wind/hail controls, and requires a composition-shingle roof in those counties to have an inspection report dated within 12 months of the effective date; this operational list is distinct from the form and bulletin seacoast-territory definitions.

Bulletin B-2021-08 applies to Texas residential property policies delivered or issued for delivery with effective dates on or after 2022-01-01; HO 01 45 is effective on the same policy-effective-date threshold, attaches to HO-3, and controls a conflict only when attached.

Texas wind/hail deductible configuration is constrained by B-2021-08: percentage deductibles may be 1%-5% of Coverage A, with a 10% seacoast maximum, and a flat dollar deductible may not be below the all-other-perils deductible; the amendment and rate rule must be filed and approved or deemed approved before application, and Declarations disclosure plus 30-day renewal-increase notice are required.

For an issued applicable HO 01 45 policy, a windstorm-or-hail loss uses only the separate wind/hail deductible; mixed covered-peril damage uses separate deductibles when attributable portions can be determined and otherwise only the larger deductible applies.

Texas's residual-market wind/hail exclusion route requires referral and a signed acknowledgment at binding; under HO 01 45, the policy result additionally depends on Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage and an attached exclusion endorsement, and T.1 does not apply when wind/hail is excluded this way.

Texas permits up to $25,000 of HO 04 90 water-backup limit without referral only when there has been no water-backup claim in five years; two or more such claims in five years makes the endorsement outside appetite while allowing the underlying policy without it, and a finished below-grade basement needs a battery-backed sump pump for a limit over $10,000.

A water-backup request above $25,000 is a matrix referral and enterprise senior authority reaches $50,000, subject to Texas's separate claim, sump, and one-referral senior controls; the matrix independently makes three or more paid water claims of any type in five years a non-clearable entire-risk hard stop.

HO 04 90 default payment terms depend on the selected edition: 2010-10 provides a $5,000 per-policy-period sublimit within the applicable A/B/C limits and a separate $500 deductible, while 2026-01 provides a $10,000 sublimit and a separate $1,000 deductible; in either edition, W.3 displaces the Section I Declarations deductible for covered endorsement loss.

Texas requires senior referral for two or more paid property claims in three years and for any mold, continuous-seepage, or foundation-movement claim; a prior liability claim involving a dog bite, trampoline, or unfenced pool also requires referral and a completed liability supplement.
Every cleared referral must document the condition, clearing authority level, specific facts relied on, and date; without the recorded basis it is treated as unbound authority in audit.

For an issued, attached, and applicable HO 01 45 endorsement, T.1 implements Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 and amends HO-3 2018-09 S.5 so a windstorm-or-hail loss receives only the separate windstorm/hail deductible rather than the all-other-perils deductible.

The Texas residual-market wind/hail exclusion route has distinct controls: G.4 requires a signed acknowledgment at binding for the operational seacoast/residual-market path, matrix R.3 requires referral, and issued-form T.7 additionally requires Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage and attachment of the applicable exclusion endorsement before T.1 does not apply.

When either compatible HO 04 90 edition is attached to HO-3, W.1 supplies the limited direct-physical-loss write-back for the A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event category, while W.4 preserves the A.1 flood/surface-water and A.2 subsurface-water exclusions; Texas G.3 binding thresholds remain separate underwriting constraints.

For a verified attached HO 04 90, 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it, whereas 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01; attachment, exact endorsement edition, policy-written date, and endorsement Declarations must be established before stating edition-specific contract terms.

Only HO 04 90 2026-01 adds a finished-below-grade coverage condition: at the time of loss, an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device must serve the sewer line; that condition does not appear in 2010-10.

For HO 04 90 water-backup loss, 2010-10 W.6 and 2026-01 W.7 each leave Coverage A/B settlement on the attached policy basis and settle Coverage C at actual cash value unless the endorsement Declarations state otherwise.

Texas G.3's $5,000 HO 04 90 base-sublimit reference matches the 2010-10 default but conflicts with the $10,000 default in 2026-01; the supplied guide and referral matrix do not provide a resolution or amend the selected issued endorsement terms.

Texas G.3's battery-backed-sump requirement is a pre-bind control only for a finished basement below grade and a requested limit above $10,000, while 2026-01 W.6 is an at-loss serving-sewer backflow-device condition for any finished-below-grade residence; neither test substitutes for the other and W.6 does not apply to 2010-10.

Both HO 04 90 editions withhold endorsement coverage when the backup, overflow, or discharge resulted from the insured's known pre-loss failure to maintain the serving sewer line, drain, sump, or sump pump and a reasonable person would have remedied it.
